content.text:
The image shows a five-membered imidazole ring with these substituents:

- N3 is the top-left "N", double-bonded to C2.
- C2 is the left carbon and carries a methyl group, drawn as a line going left.
- N1 is the bottom "NH".
- C5 is the bottom-right carbon and carries Br.
- C4 is the top-right carbon and carries NO2.
- The C4=C5 bond is double.

Writing the SMILES by going around the ring: Cc1nc([N+](=O)[O-])c(Br)[nH]1. This has the methyl carbon, then c1 (C2), then n (N3), then c with the nitro group (C4), then c with Br (C5), then [nH] closing the ring back to C2.

The name of this compound is 5-bromo-2-methyl-4-nitro-1H-imidazole.

SMILES: Cc1nc([N+](=O)[O-])c(Br)[nH]1
